messages.body_plain:
Hi Philip,

Great that you're digging into this!

What I've done is generate stubs for all the GNU R API methods into this Java package:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/tree/master/tools/gnur-runtime/src/main/java/org/renjin/gnur/api

So that things compile at least, and then we can implement the most-used methods as needed.

You can find the stub for the Rf_ScalarReal function here:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/master/tools/gnur-runtime/src/main/java/org/renjin/gnur/api/Rinternals.java#L1586-1586

There isn't a great source of documentation for the GNU R API beyond the GNU R source itself:
https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/e5b21d0397c607883ff25cca379687b86933d730/src/include/Rinlinedfuns.h#L599

but Hadley has a partial guide in his Advanced R book:
http://adv-r.had.co.nz/C-interface.html

The ScalarXX functions basically create vectors of length one from the given scalar arguments.

So you can update the stub in Rinternals.java

public static SEXP Rf_ScalarReal(double p0) {
  throw new UnimplementedGnuApiMethod("Rf_ScalarReal");
}
to the following:
public static SEXP Rf_ScalarReal(double x) {
  return new DoubleArrayVector(x);
}
And that should be enough.

If you can take a second to update the ScalarXXX functions as part of the pull request that would be great!

Best,
Alex

No, NaN treatment is the same, but often what happens is that there is a bug somewhere in Renjin somewhere that generates an NA instead of the correct value, and then this value gets passed around for a few function calls until it finally hits a function that checks its' inputs, at which point an error is thrown.

This makes it hard to debug because the site of the actual bug can be miles away from the function that finally throws an error.

If you can boil down your script to something trivial, perhaps just the first 3 rows of your dataset with masked column names, for example, then you can open an issue on GitHub and I can take a closer look.

Best,
Alex
